quests.instruction: Frogs croak and dragonflies skim over a small, shallow patch of still fresh water. What is this place?
quests.hint: Water lilies often float on top of it.
quests.explanation: A pond is a small body of still water, shallow enough for sunlight to reach the bottom. Plants grow there, and many animals live in and around it.
quests.funFact: Dragonflies spend the early part of their lives underwater before they grow wings.

quests.instruction: Little round stones along a riverbank feel smooth. What made them so smooth?
quests.hint: Think about what rubs stones together for years and years.
quests.explanation: Moving water rolls stones against each other and wears off their sharp edges bit by bit. Over time they turn smooth and round.
quests.funFact: Some river pebbles have been tumbling along for thousands of years.

quests.instruction: Which mountain has an opening at the top where hot melted rock can burst out?
quests.hint: People stay far away when it is waking up.
quests.explanation: Deep underground, rock can melt into magma. When it escapes through an opening it is called lava.
quests.funFact: Iceland has many active volcanoes.

quests.instruction: You walk across grass early in the morning and your shoes get wet from tiny drops that were not there last night. What are they?
quests.hint: They form on cool surfaces when the night air chills.
quests.explanation: At night the air cools and some of the water vapor in it turns into tiny droplets on grass and leaves. We call these dew.
quests.funFact: Namib Desert beetles collect fog droplets on their backs and drink them.

quests.instruction: On a chilly morning a thick gray mist hangs low over the field, and you can barely see the far fence. What is it?
quests.hint: It is like a cloud that has settled down on the ground.
quests.explanation: Fog is made of tiny water droplets hanging in the air close to the ground. It often forms when the air is cool and damp.
quests.funFact: Fog usually melts away as the morning Sun warms the air.

quests.instruction: Over millions of years a river has carved a very deep, narrow valley with steep rock walls. What is this landform?
quests.hint: Picture a river slowly sawing into rock for ages.
quests.explanation: Flowing water can cut into rock bit by bit. After millions of years it carves a deep canyon.
quests.funFact: The Grand Canyon in the USA is about 446 kilometers long.

quests.instruction: This forest is warm, gets rain almost every day, and is crowded with tall trees, vines, and colorful birds. What is it?
quests.hint: Think hot and humid all year round.
quests.explanation: Rainforests stay warm and wet all year, so plants grow fast. Layers of leaves create homes for many different animals.
quests.funFact: Rainforests cover only a small part of Earth, yet they are home to a huge number of species.

quests.instruction: Under warm, shallow sea water, tiny animals build a colorful rocky structure where fish hide. What is it?
quests.hint: It looks like stone or plants, but it is built by animals.
quests.explanation: Coral reefs are built by tiny animals called corals. Fish, crabs, and turtles find food and shelter among them.
quests.funFact: Coral reefs cover less than 1% of the ocean floor but shelter about a quarter of sea life.

quests.instruction: A squirrel buries a hard little nut with a rough cap, and the forgotten ones sprout into big trees. What is the nut?
quests.hint: It comes from an oak tree.
quests.explanation: Acorns are the seeds of oak trees. Squirrels bury them for later, and the ones they forget may sprout.
quests.funFact: One oak tree can drop thousands of acorns in a year.

quests.instruction: A table is made from the hard inner part of a tree trunk. What is that material?
quests.hint: Rings in a cut stump can tell you how many years the tree lived.
quests.explanation: Wood is the strong inner part of tree trunks and branches. People use it for furniture, paper, and fire, so we should use it wisely.
quests.funFact: A cut tree trunk has one ring for each year the tree lived.

quests.instruction: Potters shape bowls from a soft, sticky earth that turns hard after baking. What is it?
quests.hint: It is found along riverbanks and feels slippery when wet.
quests.explanation: Clay is very fine soil that is sticky when wet and hard after heating. People have made bowls and bricks from it for thousands of years.
quests.funFact: Some of the oldest clay pots ever found are more than 10,000 years old.

quests.instruction: Along the shore you find a hard, curly covering that once protected a soft-bodied sea animal. What is it?
quests.hint: A snail or a clam once lived inside.
quests.explanation: Animals like snails and clams make their own shells for protection. The shell grows bigger as the animal grows.
quests.funFact: Empty shells sometimes become homes for hermit crabs.

quests.instruction: A bird gathers twigs and grass to make a cozy home for its eggs. What is the home called?
quests.hint: Often it sits high in a tree, away from hungry animals on the ground.
quests.explanation: Birds build nests to keep eggs warm and safe, and later to shelter their chicks.
quests.funFact: Weaverbirds knot grass into hanging nests.

quests.instruction: Which sweet food do bees make from flower nectar?
quests.hint: Bees store it in tiny wax cells.
quests.explanation: Bees collect nectar and store it in wax cells, where it slowly thickens into honey. Bees eat it, especially when flowers are scarce.
quests.funFact: Bees fan their wings over nectar to help it dry into honey.

quests.instruction: A soft green carpet grows on damp rocks and tree trunks in shady, wet places. What is it?
quests.hint: It likes shade and wet spots, and it has no flowers.
quests.explanation: Moss is a small plant that soaks up water through its whole body. It grows best where it is damp and shady.
quests.funFact: Moss has no true roots; it holds on with tiny threads.

quests.instruction: Each morning the Sun appears on the same side of the sky. Which direction is that?
quests.hint: Where the day begins.
quests.explanation: The Sun rises in the east and sets in the west because Earth spins. It only looks like the Sun is moving.
quests.funFact: In the morning, shadows point toward the west.

quests.instruction: A huge river of ice sits on land in cold mountains and slides very slowly downhill. What is it?
quests.hint: It moves so slowly you could not see it creep.
quests.explanation: Glaciers form where more snow falls than melts. The snow packs into ice that flows slowly downhill under its own weight.
quests.funFact: Much of Earth's fresh water is locked up in glaciers and ice sheets.

quests.instruction: Wind piles sand into rolling hills in the desert. What are they called?
quests.hint: They creep and change shape when the wind blows.
quests.explanation: Wind carries sand grains and drops them in piles. Dunes can slowly shift across the desert over time.
quests.funFact: Some desert dunes are taller than skyscrapers.

quests.instruction: Which living thing pops up after rain in damp, shady spots and is neither a plant nor an animal?
quests.hint: Never pick or taste wild ones; just look.
quests.explanation: Mushrooms are fungi, a group separate from plants and animals. Fungi do not make food from sunlight; they feed on dead material.
quests.funFact: Some wild mushrooms are poisonous, so look but never taste.

quests.instruction: An insect has six legs. Which creature is an insect?
quests.hint: Count the legs: three on each side.
quests.explanation: Insects have six legs and three body parts. Spiders have eight legs, and snails have no legs at all.
quests.funFact: A ladybug's bright spots warn hungry birds that it tastes bad.

quests.instruction: Wind blowing across the sea pushes the water into rolling ridges that crash on the shore. What are they?
quests.hint: Surfers wait for the best ones.
quests.explanation: Wind blowing over the sea surface pushes the water into waves. Stronger winds make bigger waves.
quests.funFact: Waves carry energy across the water, but the water itself mostly moves in small circles.

quests.instruction: A bee leaves a flower dusted with a fine yellow powder. What is the powder?
quests.hint: Some people sneeze when lots of it floats in the air.
quests.explanation: Pollen helps flowers make seeds. Bees and wind carry it from one flower to another.
quests.funFact: Pollen grains are so small you need a microscope to see their shapes.

quests.instruction: A small wriggly creature munches leaves all day and later turns into a butterfly. What is it?
quests.hint: Before its big change, it makes a hard case around itself.
quests.explanation: A caterpillar is a young butterfly. It eats leaves to grow, makes a chrysalis, and later comes out with wings.
quests.funFact: A monarch caterpillar grows to thousands of times its hatching weight.

quests.instruction: In freezing weather, dripping water freezes into a long pointed spike hanging from a roof. What is it?
quests.hint: A warm sunny hour can make it drip until it is gone.
quests.explanation: Water drips from a slightly warm surface and freezes again in cold air as it hangs. More dripping adds length.
quests.funFact: Icicles grow longest when days are a little warm and nights are freezing.

quests.instruction: A small animal scuttles sideways along the beach and has two pinching claws. What is it?
quests.hint: Sideways is its favorite direction.
quests.explanation: Crabs walk sideways because of how their legs bend. They have a hard shell and use their claws to grab food.
quests.funFact: Crabs can regrow a lost claw over time.

quests.instruction: This huge sea animal is not a fish. It breathes air through a blowhole on top of its head. Which one is it?
quests.hint: It rises to the surface to take a breath.
quests.explanation: Whales are mammals. They breathe air and feed their babies milk, even though they live in the sea.
quests.funFact: Blue whales are the largest animals known to have ever lived.

quests.instruction: Long green-brown strands sway in the sea and give small fish places to hide. What are they?
quests.hint: Some kinds are even used to wrap sushi.
quests.explanation: Seaweed is a kind of algae that makes food from sunlight in the sea. Many sea animals use it for food and shelter.
quests.funFact: Giant kelp can grow about half a meter in a single day.

quests.instruction: Two of these are landforms. Which one is not?
quests.hint: You cannot stand on it or climb it, however tall you are.
quests.explanation: Landforms are shapes in the ground that you can walk across or climb. A cloud floats in the sky and is made of tiny water droplets or ice crystals.
quests.funFact: Fog is simply a cloud that touches the ground.

quests.instruction: Which of these can make its own food using sunlight?
quests.hint: It stays in one place and soaks up light with its leaves.
quests.explanation: Plants like ferns use sunlight, water, and air to make food in their leaves. Animals and fungi have to find their food.
quests.funFact: Ferns make tiny spores instead of seeds.

quests.instruction: A sunny open field is full of grasses and wildflowers, with butterflies drifting above. What is this place?
quests.hint: Butterflies drift over it all summer.
quests.explanation: Meadows are open grassy areas full of wildflowers. They give insects nectar and pollen and feed grazing animals.
quests.funFact: Many meadow insects, like bees and butterflies, help flowers make seeds.
